name: session-create-supplied-login

graded_by.test: core/internal/httpapi/sessions_test.go — TestACreateWithALoginSendsItInConnectAuthAndNotTheStoredCredential: the fake worker's connect carries user and auth {password} from the login, never the stored credential, and the answer carries no trace of it
core/internal/session/create_test.go — TestALoginOnATargetWithNoStoredCredentialIsNotRefused409: no stored credential resolves and the create is still 201

description: A login supplied on session create: connection new, with login {user, auth {kind password, password}}, opens a session whose connection authenticates with that account and password and nothing else. The core does not resolve a stored credential for such a request, so a target no credential resolves for (input target_no_cred_id) is not refused 409 no_resolving_credential, and credential_choice_required never answers it: the login is the operator's explicit choice (Contract §12). On the wire to the worker nothing changes: connect.user is login.user and connect.auth is {kind password, password}, the branch a stored password uses (C3/control-connect-supplied-login). The password is never stored (not in bbolt, a manifest, the spool, a log, an error message or an audit value), and the answer carries no field of the login. Every credential value in a fixture is the synthetic constant, which authenticates nowhere, so a run cannot grade this against a real target: only the core's own tests do.

recording.warning_text: This session is recorded byte-perfect. Anything typed will be stored as-is.
